outcome: Vaginal birth with episiotomy and/or instrumental birth interventions
Unplanned cesarean section without episiotomy and/or instrumental interventions
Unplanned cesarean section after episiotomy and/or instrumental interventions
cohort: 5459 primiparous women from the 1973-1978 cohort of the Australian Longitudinal Study on Women's Health
finding: Several biopsychosocial factors, including chronic hypertension, perceived length of labor, private health insurance, induced labor, pre-pregnancy weight, maternal age, and maternal height, were associated with increased likelihood of labor interventions.
mod_finding: The study found that vaginal births with episiotomy and/or instrumental interventions were more likely among women with certain risk factors, while unplanned cesarean sections without episiotomy and/or instrumental interventions were associated with different risk factors.
